full_judgment: 34. On the question  Of the letter Ext. 2(w) the receipt of which also has been denied by the.-defendant Company, the plaintiff has proved two documents, namely; Ext. 7(b) dated 13-7-53 which is a postal registration receipt of a registered letter, and Ext. 8(b) dated14-7-53, a postal acknowledgment receipt of a registered letter. The acknowledgment receipt also bears a stamp of Gladstone Wyllie & Company Limited. It is in the evidence of Mr. Grantham that the seal used by them is of different nature than the one which was used in Ext. 8(b). Having regard to Ext. 7(b) which shows that a letter was sent by registered post to Gladstone Wyllie & Company Limited, there arises a presumption according to the provision of section 27 of the General Clauses Act that the letter duly reached the addressee and this presumption is further strengthened by the (acknowledgment receipt Ext. 8(b). There is no doubt that a letter was posted on the 13th of July, 1953 addressed to Gladstone Lyall &. Company Ltd. at Chittagong Office of Gladstone Wyllie & Company Limited. Nothing has been produced ion behalf of the defendant Company to show that they did not receive the letter allege a by the plaintiff. Although Gladstone Lyall & Company was not doing any business at Chittagong and was not there. Gladstone Wyllie & Company Ltd. were representing them in connection with all matters relating to the plaintiff's Golepahar Bungalows. In that view of the matter, delivery of the letter addressed to Gladstone Lyall & Company Limited at the office of Gladstone Wyllie & Company Limited, Chittagong may be taken to be proper delivery. Under the circumstances, if we consider Ext. 8(b) along with Ext. 7 (b) and take note of the fact that there had been no rebutting evidence produced on behalf of the defendant, we feel inclined to accept the plaintiff's case that plaintiff, as a matter of fact, had sent a letter dated 13-7-53 of which Ext. 2 (w) is a copy.
